sentiment_reasoning: A triple collision of forces defines this session: the Fed's hawkish hold with 3 dissenters wanting a hike sent the Dow down 1,100 points yesterday, the US-Iran military escalation drove Brent above $89 threatening to reignite inflation, and a $1T chip stock selloff on SK Hynix earnings disappointment pressures the AI trade. However, MSFT's Azure $100B milestone and futures recovering 0.3-0.6% provide partial offset. Net bearish tilt with high two-way volatility.

summary.gist: The market is caught in a three-front war: an inflation scare from surging oil prices after US strikes on Iran, a bond market revolt pushing the 30Y yield to a multidecade 5.20%, and a trillion-dollar chip selloff questioning AI capex sustainability. Microsoft's blowout Azure quarter is the lone bright spot, but Meta's 8% premarket plunge proves the AI spending scrutiny is real. Today's GDP and PCE data at 8:30 AM will either validate the Fed hawks or give bulls ammunition — this is the session's fulcrum.

executive_summary: Markets attempt a modest recovery Thursday after the Dow's worst day since April 2025, with futures up 0.3-0.6% ahead of critical GDP and PCE data at 8:30 AM ET. The Fed held rates at 3.50-3.75% in a 9-3 vote, but three hawkish dissenters and a 30-year Treasury yield at 5.20% signal the bond market is pricing in rate hikes. Overnight US strikes on a dozen Iranian targets after an intercepted IRGC missile attack on US forces in Jordan sent Brent crude above $89 and reignited energy-inflation fears. The chip sector bled over $1 trillion this week after SK Hynix's record profits missed sky-high expectations, dragging Nvidia and memory names. Microsoft's Azure crossing $100B in annual revenue and 8% after-hours pop provides a counterweight, but Meta's earnings miss and 8% premarket drop underscores that not all AI bets are paying off equally.

macro_events.title: Fed Holds Rates 3.50-3.75% — Three Dissenters Want Hike
macro_events.causal_chain: Fed holds at 3.50-3.75% in 9-3 vote → 3 members dissent favoring 25bp hike → signals internal division on inflation → bond market reprices: 30Y yield surges to 5.20% multidecade high, 10Y to 4.67% → rate-sensitive sectors (REITs, utilities, homebuilders) face valuation compression → mortgage rates climb further → housing market cools → consumer spending pressure → but higher yields attract foreign capital → DXY firms to 101 → emerging market FX weakens
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US domestic, global bond markets, EM currencies
macro_events.historical_analog: June 2023 skip — Fed held while signaling future hikes, 10Y rose 40bp over next month. Current dynamic is more hawkish given 3 actual dissents.
macro_events.counterargument: GDP tracking ~1.5-2.0% suggests economy is moderating naturally; PCE may come in soft enough to vindicate the hold and calm bond vigilantes.

affected_tickers.reason: Bond prices inversely correlated with yields; 30Y at 5.20% is multidecade high
Utility dividend yields less attractive vs 5%+ risk-free rate
Higher rates boost NIM but increase credit risk on commercial RE exposure
Homebuilders pressured by rising mortgage rates

macro_events.title: US Strikes Dozen Iranian Targets After Intercepted IRGC Missile Attack
macro_events.causal_chain: IRGC launches ballistic missiles at US forces in Jordan → all intercepted → Trump orders retaliatory strikes on southern Iran (Bandar Abbas, Kish Island) → Brent crude surges 7% above $89 → Strait of Hormuz chokepoint risk: 21% of global oil trade + 20% of LNG transits → war-risk insurance premiums spike on VLCCs → Asian refiners may reroute via Cape of Good Hope (+12-14 days, +$2M/trip) → Qatar LNG to Europe at risk → European natural gas futures rise → defense stocks rally on weapons restocking demand → airline fuel costs surge → consumer inflation expectations tick up
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Middle East, Persian Gulf, global energy markets, European energy security
macro_events.historical_analog: Sep 2019 Abqaiq attack — Brent surged 15% in 24 hours, tanker stocks ran 20-35% in one week. Current situation involves sustained US-Iran military exchanges (Day 152 of conflict) rather than one-off attack.
macro_events.counterargument: Markets have partially priced in Iran conflict risk over 5 months; both sides have avoided targeting oil infrastructure directly; ceasefire negotiations could resume if diplomatic channels reopen.

affected_tickers.reason: Higher crude prices directly boost upstream revenue; $89 Brent = significant margin expansion
Integrated oil major benefits from crude above $85

Jet fuel cost surge compresses airline margins; fuel is 25-30% of opex
Same fuel cost headwind as DAL; Middle East route disruptions add operational costs

macro_events.title: Chip Sector Sheds $1 Trillion — AI Spending Reckoning
macro_events.causal_chain: SK Hynix reports record KRW 60.5T operating profit but misses KRW 64T consensus → market punishes miss despite near-6x YoY growth → signals expectations have outrun reality → SK Hynix -19%, Samsung -9% in Seoul → contagion hits US: NVDA, MU, AMD all pressured → $1T+ wiped from global chip market cap → investors question whether hyperscaler AI capex ($80B MSFT + $75B GOOG = unprecedented) can generate adequate returns → Meta's Q2 earnings miss reinforces AI ROI doubts → but MSFT Azure $100B proves some AI bets are paying off → market begins differentiating AI winners from laggards
macro_events.geographic_dimension: South Korea, US, Taiwan, global semiconductor supply chain
macro_events.historical_analog: Jan 2022 Netflix-led growth selloff — once one high-multiple name cracks, sector-wide multiple compression follows. Difference: current AI capex is real and generating revenue (Azure), unlike 2000 dot-com.
macro_events.counterargument: Structural AI demand is intact — Microsoft's $80B capex and Azure $100B revenue proves ROI. SK Hynix miss is about overshoot expectations, not demand destruction. Corrections in bull markets create buying opportunities.

affected_tickers.reason: Bellwether for AI hardware; sentiment contagion from memory chip miss even though GPU demand intact
Direct competitor to SK Hynix in HBM; memory pricing concern
MI300 ramp competes for same hyperscaler budgets under scrutiny
Azure $100B milestone + earnings beat validates AI capex thesis; counterexample to META miss

macro_events.title: Q2 GDP Advance Estimate and June PCE Data Release at 8:30 AM ET
macro_events.causal_chain: Atlanta Fed GDPNow tracking 1.54% for Q2 (down from 2.1% Q1) → if GDP comes in below 1.5% while PCE runs hot → stagflation narrative gains traction → bond yields could spike further → equity risk premium expands → if GDP above 2.0% with cool PCE → goldilocks relief rally, VIX drops below 18 → most likely scenario: soft GDP (1.5-1.8%) with stable PCE → modest relief but no conviction rally
macro_events.historical_analog: Q1 2025 GDP surprise — came in at -0.3% vs +0.3% expected, triggered 2% SPX decline in one session before tariff-context was understood.
macro_events.counterargument: Even a weak GDP print may be dismissed as backward-looking if leading indicators (PMIs, claims) remain resilient.

affected_tickers.reason: Directional move depends entirely on GDP/PCE combination
Weak GDP = flight to safety bid; hot PCE = further selling
Stagflation scenario favors gold as real rate hedge
